26.0.0.en: The Lord completes the commandments that the people are to begin to apply when they enter and settle in the land He gives them.

26.1.0.en: The one presenting the firstfruits must put them in a basket and carry them to the place where the house of the Lord is. The firstfruits were presented at the Feast of Pentecost (Ex 23:16, Lev 27:26), and if that was not possible, they were presented at any time.

26.2.0.en: When the one presenting the firstfruits reaches the place, he hands the basket to the priest serving in those days and makes a verbal confession before the priest that he has indeed entered and possessed the land that the Lord promised the fathers of the people to give them. By this, every presenter of firstfruits from the people of Israel acknowledges that the Lord God is the one to whom credit is due for their possession of the land and its good things, from which these firstfruits come.

26.3.0.en: The priest takes the basket from the one presenting it and places it before the altar of burnt offering, and this means presenting it to the Lord.

26.4.0.en: A Syrian ("Aramean"): of the people of Aram, who lived in the north of Iraq.

26.4.1.en: Wandering ("ready to perish"): Jacob, the father of the fathers, wandered in the lands of Aram, just as Abraham had first migrated from there. The person offers a prayer of confession extending to (v. 10), in which he summarizes the Lord's dealings with His people from the time of the fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, for they belonged to the Aramean people. Then Jacob went down to Egypt to meet his son Joseph and sojourned there, and his family who accompanied him to Egypt numbered no more than 75 persons, including Jacob and Joseph and his sons. But during their stay in Egypt their number increased greatly, as did what they owned of cattle and sheep and of wealth in general.

26.5.0.en: Pharaoh took notice of the growing importance of the people of the children of Israel and feared the increase of their strength, so he stirred up persecution against them and subjected them to bitter slavery, exploiting them in works of building and farming.

26.6.0.en: The people cried out, complaining of their condition to the Lord, and the Lord heard their groaning, knowing the harshness of treatment to which they were exposed, which wearied and humiliated them.

26.7.0.en: God brought them out with power after He struck Egypt with the ten plagues, and led them by the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire. Then He split the Red Sea and they crossed over to the wilderness of Sinai, and He drowned Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea, and so saved His people from destruction.

26.8.0.en: The Lord led them on a long journey to the place where they would settle, which is the Promised Land, promised to their fathers, and it is one of the best of lands, abounding in much good.

26.9.0.en: And now, O Lord God, behold, I have brought the firstfruits of the produce of the land which You gave us, in acknowledgment of what You have done with us and Your great love toward Your people, for You are the owner of all these good things. Then he takes the firstfruits in his hands and sets them before the altar and bows down in thanksgiving and glorification.

26.10.0.en: This person enjoys the rest of the good things after presenting the firstfruits, taking care to feed the Levites, the poor, and the strangers from these good things, so that all may feel that they are one family eating from God's hand.

26.10.1.en: Thank God every day for His gifts, and take care to give some of them to the needy, because you are all members in the Body of Christ, which is the Church.

26.11.0.en: The tithes were carried to the place of the temple for two successive years, but in the third year, which was called the year of tithing, they paid the tithes in their cities and gave them to the Levites, the strangers, the orphans, and the widows to eat and be satisfied, so that it would be an opportunity for the sick and the poor who were unable to travel to the Lord's temple in Jerusalem to eat from the feasts made from the tithes for the needy and rejoice in God's gifts.

26.12.0.en: And they were to recite the confession mentioned, which extends to (v. 15), after paying the tithes. In it the one confessing declares that he has taken out what is holy (and the word "holy" means set apart) for the Lord, meaning the tithes, and has given it to the Levites, the strangers, the orphans, and the widows as the divine Law requires, and has not departed from it or ignored it.

26.13.0.en: The one presenting the tithe, or any of God's gifts, affirms at the end of the previous verse and then again at the end of this verse that he listens to the voice of the Lord and acts according to what He commands him and does not turn aside from it to the customs and practices of the pagan peoples around him, and he eats of the feasts made from the tithes for the Levites, the poor, the strangers, and all the needy (ch. 14:22-29) as a fellowship of love with these groups, so that all may feel unity and there be no feeling of superiority on the part of the giver who presents the tithe over those who receive. The following is observed in these feasts.

26.13.1.en: "I have not eaten of it in my mourning," that is, he has not eaten of the holy food which those who share in mourning for the dead are not permitted to eat. Likewise it was among the customs of the pagan peoples to present to the god of fertility from the produce of the fields, and they mourned in remembrance of his death and gathered to eat of the produce presented to him on this occasion of remembrance; he does not take part in these pagan customs.

26.13.2.en: "Nor have I taken away ought thereof for any unclean use," the law of purity that bound the children of Israel to observe it when eating of the holy things did not exist among the pagan peoples, who set no value on bodily purity. But he, as a devout Jew, keeps purity when eating of the holy things. Uncleanness means being defiled by burying a dead person or by uncleanness for any other reason.

26.13.3.en: "Nor given ought thereof for the dead," that is, he has not spent from the money holy to God on buying shrouds or any necessities for burying the dead, and likewise he has not offered from it to the false pagan gods, who are considered dead, that is, he has not offered from it to idols.

26.14.0.en: A prayer to the Lord after presenting the confession, asking Him to look down from heaven and bless His people and bless the land that He gave him and that He promised to the fathers.

26.14.1.en: Be careful, when you eat and drink and enjoy the good things of God, that your heart be pure from all evil, so do not judge anyone or hate him, and offer repentance for your wicked thoughts and every uncleanness, and you will rejoice in God's gifts.

26.15.0.en: Moses stresses to the people the importance of obeying all the commandments they have heard, and that this obedience be not only in outward performance but with all feeling and love.

26.16.0.en: You have already made a decision to follow the Lord and to walk in His commandments, statutes, and judgments, and to listen to all His teachings and submit to His commands, and not to walk in misleading ways like the other peoples.

26.17.0.en: And the Lord has promised you that you will be a holy nation to Him, which He attributes to Himself, and that He will be its leader and protector, as He promised your fathers before.

26.18.0.en: The Lord makes you a distinguished people, exalted in rank above all peoples, who acknowledge your good conduct and good reputation, so that you will be the object of praise of all the nations and have an exalted name linked to the name of the Lord, as it is said of you, "the people of God." And the peoples will marvel at the honor that has come to you, and you will become a people consecrated to the service of the Lord and the object of His love and care.

26.18.1.en: Obedience is your way to enjoy all of God's blessings, even if the commandments seem hard, but trust that they are the most fitting thing for your life, and you will receive blessings on earth because of them and glories in heaven that cannot be expressed. Writing the Law, with the blessings and the curses

27.0.s.en: (1) Writing the Law and building the altar

27.0.0.en: Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people to keep the divine commandments that the Lord gives them.

27.1.0.en: You shall plaster them with plaster: build them and coat them with lime.

27.1.1.en: Moses commanded the people that after they cross the Jordan River into the land the Lord is giving them, they should take large stones, set them up, and cover them with lime.

27.2.0.en: And they are to write on these stones all the words of the Law when they cross the Jordan, so that the Lord may help them to possess the land that He is giving them, which flows with many good things.

27.3.0.en: You shall whitewash them with lime: cover them with plaster.

27.3.1.en: Mount Ebal: today called Imad ad-Din, it lies north of the valley in which is the city of Nablus, which was anciently Shechem.

27.3.2.en: The Lord affirms a second time that after they cross the Jordan River they are to set up these stones and that they be set up on Mount Ebal and plastered with lime, and both Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim, which will be mentioned later, enjoy a position in the middle of the holy lands, so that they are at the least possible distance from the edges of the land of Israel, so that all the tribes may make pilgrimage to them.

27.4.0.en: In addition to the stones on which you write the Law, you must build an altar to the Lord, also of stones, without dressing those stones with a chisel or an axe, but they are to be set as they are, and Joshua carried this out (Josh 8:30, 31). The altar here points to Christ, who is symbolized by Daniel in his vision (Dan 2:34) by the stone cut out without hands, for Christ was born without the seed of man.

27.5.0.en: He affirms again that the stones with which the altar is built are to be in their natural form, without any attempt to dress them with any tool.

27.6.0.en: And the offerings of thanksgiving to the Lord are presented, which are the peace offerings, which also signify rejoicing in the Lord and the offerer's gratitude for His great work done for him. It is the sacrifice of which a part is given to the priests to eat, which is the Lord's portion, and a part is eaten by the one offering the sacrifice, as a sign of the fellowship that believers live with God, and this is a type of the sacrament of Communion.

27.7.0.en: As the elders joined Moses in conveying the Lord's directions to the people, the priests join him here in leading the people and helping them to live in fellowship with the Lord. They make the people understand that, now that they have become a people chosen by the Lord and set apart for His worship and for bearing His care, they must listen to the voice of the Lord their God and obey His commandments that He commands them now.

27.7.1.en: It is noted in the preceding ten verses that God cares for His people after their entering the Promised Land, that they may abide in His word and worship and not be influenced by the laws of pagan worship nor take part in them out of courtesy to the nations around them; therefore He asked two things of them:

27.7.2.en: 1- Writing the Law on a wall or on pillars of stone, so that when they pass by it they read it and remember the word of God and hold fast to His laws.

27.7.3.en: 2- Setting up an altar of stones so that they remember that their worship is offered to God alone, whose Law is written beside this altar, and that they not offer sacrifices to any other god; for this altar is not for offering sacrifices upon it but a constant reminder of the worship of God, while the sacrifices are offered on the bronze altar in the tabernacle of meeting. With these verses the third sermon of Moses, which began from chapter twelve, ends. After that begins the concluding part, which includes the blessings and the curses, the song of Moses, the handing over of leadership to Joshua and the Levites, the writing of the Law, and then the death of Moses.

27.7.4.en: Read the Bible every day so that you learn the word of God, meditate on it, and apply it in your life, and remain a child of God, so that you are not influenced by the thoughts of the world around you, and your heart worships Him in the Church and is not occupied with the gods of the world, which are money and position......

27.8.0.en: Moses commanded the people to arrange their ranks and stand in a particular order after crossing the Jordan River, in order to recite the blessings and the curses.

27.9.0.en: Mount Gerizim: it is opposite Mount Ebal, which was mentioned in (v. 4), and is called today Mount at-Tur, and lies south of the valley in which is the city of Nablus (Map 18). He divides the tribes into two parts: six tribes on one side stand on Mount Gerizim, and they are the tribes of Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, which includes the two tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, and Benjamin. This signifies that some of the people obtain the blessings, and they are those who obey the commandments of God and His Law; it is not meant that these tribes alone receive the blessings, but those from all the tribes who obey the word of God.

27.10.0.en: And the other six tribes stand on Mount Ebal as a symbolic indication of those upon whom the curses fall, and they are the tribes of Reuben, Zebulun, Gad, Asher, Dan, and Naphtali. What is meant here by pronouncing the blessings and the curses is the people's declaration that whoever does righteousness, the blessing comes upon him, while whoever disobeys and walks in evil, the curse comes upon him.

27.10.1.en: From here came the symbolic significance of dividing the people into two groups, for there will always be those who do good, as there will also be those who do evil.

27.11.0.en: The Levites: the priests are meant, who are from the tribe of Levi, as is clear from (Josh 8:33-35). The tribes stood at the two mountains, and those who pronounced the curses and the blessings were the priests standing in the middle of the valley, for they are the ones who light the way before the people and alert them to what is righteousness deserving the blessing and what is evil deserving the curse.

27.12.0.en: From this verse to the end of the chapter there are 12 warning commands beginning with the word "cursed," and there is no list of blessings because they are simply the opposite of the words of the curse. For whoever errs in one of the commands is cursed, and consequently whoever does not err is blessed.

27.12.1.en: Likewise the twelve laws mentioned are not the whole Law but a chosen group symbolizing all the Lord's commandments.

27.12.2.en: After each formula that the Levites pronounce, the people answer with the word Amen, which means "truly." The first curse: the subject of this curse relates to the second of the Ten Commandments (Ex 20:4, 5), for whoever carves an image or casts one to worship it as an idol does a work abhorred by the Lord, even if it is in secret, away from the eyes of people.

27.13.0.en: The second curse relates to the fifth of the Ten Commandments, which commands the honoring of parents (Ex 20:12), and the meaning of a person's making light of his parents is that he looks upon them with disdain and contempt and treats them lightly and does not honor them.

27.14.0.en: The third curse: the landmark is the boundary of ownership that separates the property of one person from the property of his neighbor, so it is a prohibition of coveting what belongs to others, as mentioned in (Ex 20:17), that is, in the tenth of the Ten Commandments.

27.15.0.en: The fourth curse applies in its literal meaning and its symbolic meaning. The literal meaning is that a person mocks a blind man and so leads him astray from the right way, or ridicules someone with some infirmity. The figurative meaning is intended for one who deceives the simple with misleading counsel or teaches the ignorant corrupt teaching.

27.16.0.en: The fifth curse: a commandment repeated many times in this book, concerning the weak in general and those who have no human support. The Lord forbids wronging them or infringing on their rights or departing from truth and justice in judging for them.

27.17.0.en: The sixth curse: this verse and the next three verses are a group that points to forbidden sexual practices and relate to the seventh commandment (Ex 20:14). The skirt: the edge of the garment; and since husband and wife are one, it belongs to the husband as it belongs to the wife, so his father's skirt means the skirt of the garment of his father's wife, that is, committing adultery with her. This deed is abhorred by the Lord, so it is never right for a person to have relations with his father's wife, whether in his father's lifetime or after his death, for the son must not violate his father's sanctity.

27.18.0.en: The seventh curse: this heinous deed was common among the pagan peoples. The Lord warns His people against everything that takes them away from holiness and brings them down to base levels and perverse sexual practices.

27.19.0.en: The eighth curse, which is one of the forbidden marriages (see Lev 18:9, 20:17), where this was considered a shame that required the cutting off of those who commit it from the sons of their people.

27.20.0.en: The ninth curse: marrying the mother-in-law or falling with her into sin was a contemptible and unclean act whose punishment was severe, burning with fire, because she is considered his mother (Lev 20:14).

27.21.0.en: The tenth curse: this curse recalls the sixth of the Ten Commandments, which forbids killing (Ex 20:13); for the crime of murder, even if it happens in secret without the murderer being known, the Lord who knows hidden things will punish the one who commits it. The neighbor here means any member of society.

27.22.0.en: The eleventh curse: whoever sheds the blood of an innocent person, whether by taking payment for it or by sentencing him to it judicially without right, by taking a bribe in return for the judge's issuing this sentence, the curse of God falls upon him.

27.23.0.en: The twelfth curse: whoever does not care about all that the books of the Law contain of commandments, judgments, and teachings, so as to hold fast to them and apply them in his life and act according to them, is cursed by God.

27.23.1.en: From here we understand the words of the Apostle Paul in (Gal 3:10), "For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them."

27.23.2.en: Only One obeyed all the Law and fulfilled all righteousness and accepted the curse for us, hanging on the cross, although He alone is good: the Lord Jesus Christ, who moved us from the bondage of the Law to the freedom of the glory of the children of God.

27.23.3.en: The commandment is a lamp and the Law is a light that illumines our way so that we know what is good for us. The more we listen to the word of God, the more we receive the blessing and escape the curse.

27.23.4.en: The details of the blessings and the curses
